content.title: About
content.content: A chicken and vegetable quesadilla is a Mexican‑style dish consisting of a thin corn or wheat tortilla filled with sautéed chicken, fresh vegetables (bell pepper, onion, tomato) and melted cheese. It is quickly cooked on a skillet or grill, producing a crispy exterior and a juicy interior.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The word “quesadilla” comes from the Spanish “quesada,” meaning “cheesy.”
Traditional Mexican quesadillas use corn tortillas, while flour versions are popular in the United States.
The dish is commonly served with salsa, guacamole, and sour cream.
Quesadillas can be a snack or a full‑meal option.
Chicken‑filled versions appeared in the early 20th century when chicken became more affordable.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Chicken breast provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both chicken and vegetables supply B6 and B12, supporting nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Bell peppers and tomatoes are rich in vitamin C and carotenoids, which protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Melted cheese adds calcium, important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Moderate carbohydrate load
items.content: When made with a whole‑grain tortilla, the quesadilla remains relatively low in simple carbs.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese can trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk‑protein allergy.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared sauces and cheese often contain high salt levels; use them sparingly.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Chicken must be cooked thoroughly to eliminate salmonella.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese and tortilla add calories; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cut the quesadilla into wedges and eat with your hands. Serve with salsa, guacamole or sour cream, and garnish with fresh cilantro or parsley for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat in a skillet or oven to restore crispness.
